podcast.title: First 100-Watt Guitar Amp (1962)
podcast.body: In 1962, surf guitar king Dick Dale collaborated with Fender to create and produce the first ever 100-watt guitar amplifier. This was a significant achievement, allowing for a powerful, overdriven sound when set to its limits. "In 1962, surf guitar king Dick Dale worked with Fender to produce the first ever 100 watt guitar amp, a very big deal, setting everything to overdrive created a sound like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Coined "Surf Music"
podcast.body: Dick Dale is credited with coining the term "Surf Music," marking the beginning of the original surf music craze and its association with California culture. "It was Dick Dale who coined the term Surf Music, and this was the beginning of the original surf music craze and part of the obsession with California."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Fender on Stratocaster for Surf Music
podcast.body: Richard Monsour, known by his stage name Dick Dale, was a prominent figure in the emerging genre of Surf Music. Fender hired him as a consultant to broaden their customer base beyond country music. With Dale's input, the Fender Stratocaster became an indispensable element of the surf music sound. "Monsour, who used the stage name Dick Dale, was big into this budding thing called Surf Music. And with his help, the Fender Stratocaster became an essential part of that surf music sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 1

podcast.title: Lack of Top 40 Hits but Powerful Sound
podcast.body: Despite never achieving a Top 40 hit, Dick Dale's powerful guitar sound left a lasting impression on anyone who heard him play. "Now Dick Dale never had a top 40 hit, but anyone who heard him play the guitar never forgot that sound of power."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Left-Handed, Upside-Down Guitar Playing
podcast.body: Dick Dale played his guitar left-handed and upside down, developing new sounds that led him to become a consultant for the Fender Company. In this role, he tested amplifiers and portable reverb units, contributing to their development. "Dick played his guitar left handed and upside down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Legendary Surf Guitarist Participant
podcast.body: Dick Dale, recognized as a legendary surf guitarist from the 1960s, was among the seasoned musicians who played the Warped Tour. "Dick Dale, the legendary surf guitarist from the 1960s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Surf Music as a Precursor to Heavy Rock
podcast.body: Surf Music, exemplified by recordings from 1962, is identified as containing elements that could be seen as precursors to the future sound of heavy rock. "In fact, if you listen to songs like this, you can maybe hear the future of Heavy Rock. This however, is from 1962."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unique Picking Style and Gear
podcast.body: Dale developed a distinctive picking style influenced by jazz drummer Gene Krupa. He used heavy gauge strings and played through incredibly loud custom-made Fender amplifiers to achieve his sound. "He had a picking style influenced by jazz drummer Jean Croupeau. He used heavy strings and super loud custom made amps by Fender."

xref.title: Musical Influences
xref.body: Growing up in a musical family, East Bay Ray was exposed to a wide range of influences, including instrumental surf rock. His heroes included Dick Dale, George Tomscow of The Fireballs, and Scotty Moore (who played in Elvis Presley's band) due to Moore's use of echo and reverb. Ray developed a distinctive guitar sound that was appealing to hardcore fans, a style heavily influenced by surf music. "He came from a musical family and was exposed to a lot of influences growing up, and that included instrumental surf rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

xref.title: Surf Music Popularization
xref.body: The Beach Boys were noted for singing about surf culture, driving to the beach in their "little deuce coup" to catch waves, after the initial surf music craze had already begun in Southern California in the early 1960s. "And long before the beach boys sang about driving to the beach in their little discoop to catch a wave, there was Dick Dale."
